Fraudulent Vet

By: Liz Fish | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Fake Vet treats animals and orders schedule 6 drugs and gets caught on camera faking his qualifications

Unique Selling Point:
Mr. Eric Victor Du Preez submitted job applications to the SPCA in June and again in August 2025. In his second application, he falsely claimed to be a qualified NSPCA Inspector and produced what appeared to be an official Inspector’s Certificate.

On verification with the National Council of SPCAs (NSPCA), it was confirmed that:

- Mr. Du Preez has never attended or completed Inspector training with the NSPCA.
- The certificate he produced was fraudulent.
- The signatures of senior NSPCA officials appearing on the certificate were forged.

Mr. Du Preez also lied in his CVs, providing contradictory employment histories and false qualifications, including a claim of being registered with the South African Veterinary Council (SAVC) as an Animal Welfare Assistant. The SAVC has since confirmed that multiple fraud-related cases are already pending against him under other dockets. There are 6 confirmed cases pending with SAPS.

We are going to have an interview for the position with him next week. Waiting for him to confirm which date. Then we will have him arrested here at the SPCA by SAPS after the interview, where he will once again lie. We will then also open charges.

This case raises serious concerns about fraudulent misrepresentation in the animal welfare sector and the risks posed when unqualified individuals attempt to pass themselves off as Inspectors entrusted with powers of law enforcement.

Summary:
There are 6 cases against him. He posed as a Vet and ordered schedule 6 drugs after falsifying his qualifications. Used the Panarama vetinary services email and Vat number He will come to the NSPCA for the job interview which we will film under cover. After the interview outside the building the police will arrest him.
he has treated animals posing as a VET administering medicines. he has offered sterilizations. Tried to sell fake medicines to Pet shops. Lied about being a Vet at the SPCA and created a logo with that. Got onto the Veterinary Councils website and inserted his name there as a registered Vet. Posed as a State Vet using their email address, stole the Veterinary Council Registration certificate. Faked his qualifications from UNISA. Stole several email address and altered them slightly to appear legit. Stole a registered Vets details and attempted to order drugs using their details

Further information:
Here are the case numbers involving Eric Victor du Preez:
Philippi CAS 36/03/2024
Diep River CAS 20/04/2025
Grassy Park CAS 130/04/2025 - was arrested on this case
Grassy Park CAS 161/04/2025 - was arrested on this case
Lansdowne CAS 138/06/2025
Grassy Park CAS 523/06/2025.

All these cases are being investigated by Constable Madatt from Grassy Park Detectives.

The address supplied to SAPS at the time of his arrest was 10 Frank Way, Ottery.
The email he used to obtain the Registration of Veterinary Facility document from Panorama Vet Clinic

Extra Budget Items:
I need another camera in Pretoria to film Veterinary Council DenaMarie- they are in Pretoria and the shoot is in CT so it can be shot on teams but as a key interview it needs to be good quality so I need it shot professionally as it will be a substantial interview as Eric has been posing as a Vet and they have been contacted by victims and pharmacists

VO: They say trust takes years to build… and seconds to destroy.
MUSIC builds — slow, tense
(Jaco Pieterse) 00:05:40:11 — “Thank you. And when did you qualify as an SPCA inspector?”
Beat.
(Eric Du Preez) “That was in 2021…”
VO: This is Eric Du Preez He believes he’s here for a job interview at the SPCA in Cape Town.
(Jaco Pieterse) So you were saying you were 4 months at Panorama
(Eric Du Preez) Yes I did practicals there and then afterwards I did a pro bono there
VO: But this isn’t an interview - it's a sting — and it's been a tense few hours waiting to see if he would actually arrive.
(Jaco Pietrse) They have told us they have got criminal cases pending against you
( Eric Du Preez) Which cases
(Jaco Pieterse) For fraud
(Erin Bates) Do you want to respond on the allegations that you have been treating animals with falsified Veterinary qualifications
Upsound: “Anything you say can and will be held against you…”
VO: From a job interview… to handcuffs.
Who is Eric Du Preez and how did he end up here?
FADE TO BLACK
(John Brooks) He's my everything. If something is going to happen to Scotty. I don't know if how I will react. He plays a big factor in my life

Beat

VO: John Brooks and his red nose Pitbull Scotty- have been inseparable from day one.

Beat

VO: But things could have turned out very differently.

As a puppy, Scotty fell dangerously sick. John rushed him to a man calling himself “Fetch A Vet.”

( John Brooks) He looked like a vet. He looked a top notch. And, um, he then looked at Scotty, alright no, this is whats wrong with Scotty and then he described Scotty having an internal fever, and then he gave Scotty a B complex, vitamin shot.

VO: It took a few days, but Scotty pulled through. So, when his girlfriend’s dog Strika, was badly injured by a car, John knew exactly who to call.

(John Brooks): He said, all right, this is what's wrong. We need this. This and this and this medication. Uh, can we take him to the closest pharmacy?He then injected Strika, treated the wounds and from there on it was all right. But after that I told Kaylee - he looks frek sketchy. Like the car that he arrived with was falling apart, there was no bumper on the bloody car, and I said to Kaylee this is concerning, like I don't feel lekker with this oak anymore.

VO: This sketchy guy is Eric Du Preez - a self-styled vet who appears to have targeted pet owners desperate for affordable care. The perfect business plan: cheap, mobile, and only missing one tiny detail… a qualification.
Upsound (Dinamari Scholtz)‘ Goie midday
”VO: Eric first popped up on Dinamari Stoltz radar two years ago.
As Legal Affairs Director at the SA Veterinary Council, she fielded a call from a distraught woman. Her dog was gravely sick after Eric cleaned an abscessed tooth, no anaesthetic, no sterile equipment. But he did mix antibiotics in a Coke bottle – and left her to treat her agonised dog.
(Dinamari Scholtz)The initial query was about a dog, and then she contacted me about a horse. During the incident with the horse, I spoke to Mr. Du Preez on the telephone, and he indicated to me that he is allowed to practice, uh, which I of course knew was not the case
VO: Eric was not only treating animals he was ordering large quantities of medicine from Pharmacy’s and wholesale veterinary supplies, providing them with false proof of payments.

(Dinamari Scholtz) “He did forged a veterinary degree from the University of Pretoria.He also forged a registration certificate for himself as a veterinarian, as well as a facility registration certificate, ostensibly signed by our registrar.

Breather

(Erin Bates) “ Eric would casually walk into pharmacies using a fake veterinarian registration, and one of the 6 charges against him involves scamming this pharmacy out of R5000 for 200 bottles of stylpayne
(Dinamari Scholtz) Well, he gained access to a number of medications amongst them schedule five medicines, which is highly addictive. And then he tried to gain access to stylpayne pediatric syrup, which, it's not indicated for dogs.
And this stylpayne syrup can be used with sprite and another scheduled medicine to induce a high in people,
Breath

VO: The list of medication he managed to buy is extensive
So, it's little surprise that when Eric arrived with a well-stocked medical bag - Sheena Cox was delighted. He offered his services as a mobile Vet for her animal centre.
( Sheena Cox) . So he t looked like he had everything needed for, um, any veterinarian would have on the road…He did know some things he seemed like a very intelligent man
VO: Sheena also runs a grooming parlour and seriously considered going into business with Eric. After all - his whatsapp name - was SPCA Vet. And he was the first expert she thought of when one of her client’s puppies contracted the deadly parvo virus.

(Celia Vermeulen) I mean. our stress levels were up there, and, um, he came with nothing, so we had to go back to the the the van that he drove and get the parvo test. … he then put the little swab in the mouth which I have never seen. I mean, I was so stunned
VO: Parvo tests aren’t done orally and Celia Vermeulen knew enough to be alarmed when Eric used the swab in the wrong end.
(Celia Vermeulen) And he said, you know, this is definitely worms. I know when I see it, it is worms. He actually took some of the poop …and he said he will go now and test it at the SPCA

VO: Before leaving, Eric offered some sage advice:

(Celia Vermeulen) He said it was worms but if it was to be parvo, disprin and brandy. And first thing in the morning, bicarbonate of soda. I was like blown away by what I heard.

VO: A treatment plan that sounded more like a dodgy hangover remedy.

Celia raced her dogs to the SPCA, reported Eric, and demanded her money back

(Ceilia Vermeulen). He then went and said, if if I'm gonna do anything now to, blacken his name, he will sue me because they have lawyers

LINK (Erin Bates) “ Eric told several people he was a Vet at the SPCA, he even offered to do sterilizations at their premises after hours”
Breath.
VO: Did Eric begin to believe his own lies? He started applying for jobs at the SPCA- first as an Animal health technician, then as an animal inspector.

But Chief Inspector Jaco Pieterse - was onto him

(Jaco Pieterse): There were several aspects of his application that raised concern, including a fake email address that he used that linked to a well-known veterinary practice here in Cape Town. He also claimed to have been working for an SPCA that is no longer in existence.

VO: Eric faced six charges – but he’d been evading arrest for months. So Pieterse set up a job interview , and invited us, to watch him walk into his own trap.
(Jaco Pieterse) Hello. How are you? Nice to meet you. You are welcome to take a seat that side.

Okay, so let's kick off. Tell us about yourself.

(Eric Du Preez): I'm from Orkney Snork nie so I recently moved to Cape Town about a year ago….. I worked it for basically five years there by Klerksdorp SPCA before they closed down. Then I went to I worked by the State Department, veterinary clinician as animal health technician.

(Jaco Pieterse): Thank you. And when did you qualify as an SPCA inspector?

(Eric Du Preez): That was in 2021. I do have a certificate in accounting science. Then I have a certificate in animal welfare. And I'm currently busy with my diploma in animal health.

(Jaco Pieterse): And you said that you did your training at Klerksdorp SPCA?

( Eric Du Preez)“ Yeah.

VO: But Jaco had come prepared. Every reference Eric listed had already been checked — and questioned.

(Suzette Kotze) “ I can’t give him a reference with a clean heart”

(Jaco Pieterse) And he said he did his training under you

(Suzette Kotze) No he did not

(Jaco Pieterse) So we did make contact with them, and they said they don't have any record.

(Eric Du Preez): Okay. I would just follow that up by bleep

(Jaco Pieterse): So we followed up with the NSPCA with regards to your inspector status. And they say they don't have record.

(Eric Du Preez): Okay. That's strange. So how are we are we going to resolve that part?

(Jaco Pieterse): That's the certificate.

( Eric Du Preez) Yes.

(Jaco Pietrse) ” That you gave us. So what I'm saying is basically that this is the signatures on your certificate, and those are the original signatures and that it's not the same. They saying that you fraudulently made this

(Jaco Pieterse): I would never do such a thing at all.

(Jaco Pieterse): Okay, but we've got two affidavits from them saying that.

(Eric Du Preez): Ek het nie its doen nie, how would it be possible to do something like it?

LINK” (Erin Bates) So as you can hear Jaco Pieterse has just asked Eric Du Preez, You don’t have a certificate, this is the interview taking place with false documentation provided, by the applicant to the SPCA

VO As the interview continues. Law enforcement officials are on standby to make an arrest.

(Jaco Pieterse): there's also allegations that you are impersonating a veterinarian.

(Eric Du Preez): Not at all.

(Jaco Pieterse): Okay. And have you ever used, uh, forged documents to order drugs?

(Eric Du Preez) No, not at all.

(Jaco Pieterse) Veterinary drugs?

(Eric Du Preez) “Not at all
(Eric Du Preez): As I would just like to follow up all these allegations man, because that is way wrong Tomorrow or the next day you could be arrested
VO: And with that, the interview was over.

(Erin Bates) Mr Du Preez its Erin from Carte Blanche are you English or Afrikaans speaking,
(Eric Du Preez) “Why
(Erin Bates) “We want to ask you a few questions, because there are complaints against you, committing fraud by falsifying your veterinary qualifications,

Breather

COP” I am placing you under arrest for multiple cases of fraud from Grassy Park, Phillipi, Cape Town to Diep river. OK. Anything you say can and will be held against you in a court of law,
Jaco Pieterse): I thought he would get up during the interview and leave when we started questioning his credentials, but he sat through the interview as if someone must have made a mistake, not him.
(Erin Bates) Do you want to respond to allegations that you have been treating animals

VO: Accessing schedule 5 medicines is one thing - It’s another to gamble with animals’ lives
(John Brooks) He is not an actual Vet , Its absolutely shocking to think that somebody will will try to be a vet. How many more people are out there doing the same thing

VO: Eric Du Preez remained in custody for 6 weeks without bail.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Mr. Eric Victor Du Preez submitted job applications to the SPCA in June and again in August 2025. In his second application, he falsely claimed to be a qualified NSPCA Inspector and produced what appeared to be an official Inspector’s Certificate. On verification with the National Council of SPCAs (NSPCA), it was confirmed that: - Mr. Du Preez has never attended or completed Inspector training with the NSPCA. - The certificate he produced was fraudulent. - The signatures of senior NSPCA officials appearing on the certificate were forged. Mr. Du Preez also lied in his CVs, providing contradictory employment histories and false qualifications, including a claim of being registered with the South African Veterinary Council (SAVC) as an Animal Welfare Assistant. The SAVC has since confirmed that multiple fraud-related cases are already pending against him under other dockets. There are 6 confirmed cases pending with SAPS. We are going to have an interview for the position with him next week. Waiting for him to confirm which date. Then we will have him arrested here at the SPCA by SAPS after the interview, where he will once again lie. We will then also open charges. This case raises serious concerns about fraudulent misrepresentation in the animal welfare sector and the risks posed when unqualified individuals attempt to pass themselves off as Inspectors entrusted with powers of law enforcement.
